summary: Details the SONET/SDH technology-specific information needed when sending Link Management Protocol test messages. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Before using a cable, neighbors send a small test message. This memo explains how to format that test for SONET/SDH optical links.

questions: what is lmp sonet sdh test message
what are j0 j1 j2 trace bytes
subtitle: How LMP link verification works on SONET and SDH links, using trace bytes and new trace messages.

tldr.problem: LMP verifies links by sending Test messages over each data link, but on SONET/SDH links the test has to be carried in a way that suits that technology, and control plane identifiers should stay separate from transport ones.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4207 defines Verify Transport Mechanism flags for SONET/SDH (section or line DCC, or J0, J1 and J2 trace correlation) and adds trace monitoring messages that compare an expected trace value with what is received in-band.
tldr.outcome: SONET/SDH links get a defined way to carry LMP link verification. It is a Proposed Standard, was later updated by RFC 6898 and builds on RFC 4204.

facts.label: Trace Type values
facts.value: 1 to 6 (J0, J1, J2 for SONET and SDH)

today: RFC 4207 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2005, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted. It has been updated by RFC 6898 and depends on RFC 4204.

sections.title: What This Memo Adds to LMP
sections.content:
RFC 4207 is a companion to RFC 4204, the Link Management Protocol (LMP). LMP has four procedures: control channel management, link property correlation, link verification and fault management. The first two are mandatory and the last two are optional. This memo supplies the SONET/SDH technology-specific information for the link verification and link property correlation procedures.

The RFC also notes that when LMP is used with SONET/SDH, the fault management procedures may not be needed, because existing SONET/SDH mechanisms can be used.

The central idea is the trace correlation transport mechanism, defined for the J0, J1 and J2 overhead bytes. It separates the transport plane identifiers from the control plane identifiers, and it needs a new trace monitoring function that the memo defines.
sections.eli5: LMP already has a way to test cables. This memo adds the special instructions for one kind of cable, SONET/SDH fiber.

sections.title: Verify Transport Mechanisms
sections.content:
In RFC 4204, a BeginVerify message agrees on test parameters, among them the bit rate, the encoding type and the transport mechanism. The data rate is a 32-bit IEEE floating-point number in bytes per second. For SONET/SDH the encoding type must equal the value for "SDH ITU-T G.707/SONET ANSI T1.105" from RFC 3471.

The Verify Transport Mechanism is a 16-bit bit mask. Several bits can be set in BeginVerify, but only one may be set in BeginVerifyAck. The SONET/SDH flags are:

  • 0x0002 DCCS: the Test message travels over the Section/RS data communications channel using HDLC framing.
  • 0x0004 DCCL: the same over the Line/MS DCC.
  • 0x0008 J0-trace: Section/RS trace correlation.
  • 0x0040 J1-trace: STS SPE/HOVC path trace correlation.
  • 0x0080 J2-trace: VT SPE/LOVC path trace correlation.

The values 0x0001, 0x0010 and 0x0020 are reserved.
sections.eli5: The neighbors first agree how to pass the test note: write it on a special strip of the cable, or read the name tag already printed on the cable.

sections.title: Trace Correlation for Verification
sections.content:
For the DCC options, the Test message is sent over the data link exactly as defined in RFC 4204. The trace options work differently. With J0, J1 or J2 trace the Test message is not carried in the overhead bytes. It is sent over the control channel and then correlated for consistency with the pattern received in-band in the J0, J1 or J2 byte.

To make this work, the transmitting node must provide the mapping between the in-band pattern and the Test message. That is done with a new TRACE object. The Test message for these modes is the common header, a LOCAL_INTERFACE_ID, a VERIFY_ID and a TRACE object.
sections.eli5: Instead of writing the test note on the cable, the neighbor says over the phone "look for the name tag ABC on cable 3". The other side then checks the cable really carries that tag.

sections.title: The TRACE Object and Trace Messages
sections.content:
Trace monitoring lets a node use SONET/SDH capabilities. It can ask a neighbor to monitor a link for a given pattern with TraceMonitor, and the neighbor MUST report a mismatch. It can ask for the current trace value with TraceReq, and it can ask the neighbor to send a specific trace with InsertTrace.

The TRACE object (Class 21, C-Type 1) holds a 16-bit Trace Type, a 16-bit Trace Length and the Trace Message, padded with zeros to a 32-bit boundary. The padding is not counted in Trace Length. Trace Type values are 1 to 6: SONET Section Trace (J0), SONET Path Trace (J1), SONET Path Trace (J2), and the SDH equivalents. The object is non-negotiable.

The memo defines eleven messages, numbered 21 to 31, listed with the diagram below. A TraceMonitorNack uses a new ERROR_CODE C-Type 3 (TRACE_ERROR) with bits 0x01 Unsupported Trace Type and 0x02 Invalid Trace Message. A TraceMonitorNack for a mismatched value means the TraceMismatch message SHOULD NOT be sent as a result.
sections.eli5: The messages are questions and answers about name tags on the cable: "watch for this tag", "what tag do you see?", "please put this tag on", and "the tag is wrong".

sections.title: How the Trace Messages Behave
sections.content:
A node that gets a TraceMonitor request MUST answer with TraceMonitorAck or TraceMonitorNack. The Ack means the TRACE objects were processed correctly, with no trace mismatch. Later, if the in-band trace stops matching, the monitoring node reports it with a TraceMismatch message listing the affected local Interface_Ids, and the receiver MUST respond with TraceMismatchAck. One message can report several links.

A TraceReq names an interface and a Trace Type, and the reply is a TraceReport that MUST include a TRACE object for that data link, or a TraceReqNack with an ERROR_CODE. InsertTrace asks the remote node to send a trace message over a data link, and it assumes the remote knows the mapping between local and remote Interface_Ids. Once InsertTraceAck is received, TraceMismatch is used to flag a mismatch. All of these go over the control channel.
sections.eli5: If the name tag on the cable ever changes to the wrong one, a neighbor calls the other and says "cable 3 has the wrong tag", and the other must reply that he heard.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
LMP message security uses IPsec as described in RFC 4204. RFC 4207 adds no other new security considerations.

For IANA, the memo assigns LMP Message Types 21 to 31 to the eleven trace messages, TRACE as Object Class 21 (C-Type 1) and TRACE REQ as Object Class 22 (C-Type 1).
sections.eli5: The new messages are kept safe the same way as the old LMP messages, and the memo asks for new numbers for them in the official list.

items.label: DCCS
items.desc: Test message over the Section/RS DCC.

items.label: DCCL
items.desc: Test message over the Line/MS DCC.

items.label: TraceMonitor
items.desc: Asks the neighbor to monitor a link for a trace value.

items.label: TraceMonitorNack
items.desc: Request not supported or the value was wrong.

items.label: TraceMismatch
items.desc: Reports a trace mismatch on a data link.

items.label: TraceReq
items.desc: Asks for the current trace value of a link.

items.label: TraceReqNack
items.desc: Refuses a TraceReq with an error code.

items.label: InsertTrace
items.desc: Asks the neighbor to send a specific trace on a link.
